verdict_reasoning: The proposal stops at level 1b on demand. Message #1 gives one use, emptying unlogged tables after a reset, and its question about other uses has no answer in the thread. A start, an immediate stop and a second start already reach that result (already-exists-1). Four of the five non-default values have no stated use (demand-2).

brief.title: pg_resetwal: add --cluster-state option to set the pg_control state
brief.problem: pg_resetwal always writes the shut-down state to pg_control, so the next start skips crash recovery. After a reset of a crashed cluster, unlogged tables keep whatever was on disk. The only use case the author can show is getting unlogged tables reset, and he asks Michael what other use he had in mind.
brief.proposed_design: A new --cluster-state option tells pg_resetwal which state to store in pg_control instead of shut-down. Any other state makes the next start run crash recovery with no WAL to replay, so the other recovery steps still run. DB_STARTUP is excluded because the server refuses to start with it, and --dry-run shows the current and new state.
user_visible_surface: pg_resetwal option --cluster-state=state, with values shut-down (default), shut-down-in-recovery, shutting-down, in-crash-recovery, in-archive-recovery, in-production.
pg_resetwal --dry-run shows the stored state under "Current pg_control values" and the new one under "Values to be changed".
The documentation's claim that a reset of a cleanly shut down cluster leaves contents unchanged no longer holds for non-default states.
author_claims: With a non-shut-down state, the next start runs crash recovery and empties unlogged tables, shown with a 1000-row table going to 0.
A wrong state can be fixed by running pg_resetwal -f again, and the second reset loses nothing because the WAL is already gone.
A mode that changes only the state without a reset would be a different tool, because setting shut-down on a crashed cluster would skip needed recovery.
Michael Paquier suggested the option and David asked for a separate thread.
brief.thread_state: Sho Ito tested v1 and v2 and confirmed they work; Chao Li found no code issues but asked for a state-only mode, which the author declined. The use case is still open, since Michael has not answered what he had in mind.
unclear: The proposal gives no use case beyond resetting unlogged tables, and Michael's original motivation is not in the thread.
The proposal does not say what each non-default state does differently at startup, such as in-archive-recovery or shut-down-in-recovery on a standby.
The proposal does not say whether non-default states interact with other pg_resetwal options or with standby and archive recovery settings.
The tests cover only in-production and a bad value, not the other four states.
Nobody discussed whether this option belongs in pg_resetwal or in a separate pg_control editing tool.

prior_attempts.title: Add DB_IN_END_OF_RECOVERY_CHECKPOINT state for control file
prior_attempts.quote: This patch would bring some extra visibility for something that's not incorrect either on HEAD, as end-of-recovery checkpoints are the same things as shutdown checkpoints.
prior_attempts.reason: Michael Paquier argued that the current state is not incorrect, because an end-of-recovery checkpoint is a shutdown checkpoint and the code has relied on that for about 10 years. He said the change was not checked against other assumptions, such as unlogged relation reset needing a clean shutdown, and that it leaves an invalid minimum recovery point in DB_IN_ARCHIVE_RECOVERY. He added that it would make back-patching harder in a sensitive area, and the entry was closed after the thread went quiet.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P5 changed which state the server writes during the end-of-recovery checkpoint. This patch lets a user write any state offline, so startup's dependence on the stored state matters for every accepted value.

objections.title: Existing idioms already reset unlogged tables after pg_resetwal
objections.failure_scenario: A DBA resets a crashed cluster and wants unlogged tables emptied. Today they can start the server with listen_addresses = '', run pg_ctl stop -m immediate, and start again, which runs crash recovery and resets unlogged relations. The project would then keep a six-value option, docs and tests that only save this extra restart.
objections.argument: Message #1 shows one use case, emptying unlogged tables, and the author asks Michael for another, which has not arrived. An immediate stop already leaves the state in-production, so the next start runs crash recovery, the same path the option reaches. Running TRUNCATE on each unlogged table is a second existing route. The existing ways cost more steps, but they do the job, so the option adds convenience and no new capability.
objections.author_must_show: What does --cluster-state do that pg_resetwal followed by a start and pg_ctl stop -m immediate cannot, and who needs it?

precedents.title: pg_replslotdata - a tool for displaying replication slot information

critic.reasoning: A start, an immediate stop and a second start do reach crash recovery and reset unlogged tables, and the thread shows no other use. [P12] concerned a separate tool, so it should not be used as support here.

objections.title: Five of the six state values have no stated use
objections.failure_scenario: A DBA reads the docs and picks in-archive-recovery or shut-down-in-recovery on a standby, because the docs list them as valid. Startup does something the docs do not describe, and nobody in the thread can say what the intended use was. Each new DBState value then needs a matching option value with no user behind it.
objections.argument: The one example in message #1 needs only some state other than shut-down, and in-production gives that. The patch still exposes all six values, and the v2 tests cover only in-production and a bad value. Each extra value adds documented behaviour that the project must explain and keep with no demand to justify it.
objections.author_must_show: What concrete case needs each of the five values other than shut-down, and would a single "force crash recovery" switch cover the known need?

critic.reasoning: Message #1 states that the unlogged-table reset is the only known use, and in-production covers it. The thread gives no case for the other four non-default values, and the question to Michael has no answer.

other_surviving.title: Option exposes the internal DBState enum as a permanent user contract
other_surviving.failure_scenario: An operator who wants unlogged tables reset must pick one of six documented values, with no guidance on how they differ. Later, a patch that renames, splits or adds a DBState value breaks scripts that call pg_resetwal --cluster-state, and nothing fails if that patch does not update the mapping.
other_surviving.argument: The only use case shown is forcing crash recovery so unlogged tables are reset (message #1), and the documentation gives all five non-default values the same effect. DBState is internal today, and [P5] shows its values are still debated. Once documented, each value becomes a user-facing name that must stay stable across releases. A single option that forces crash recovery at next start would cover the shown need without exposing the enum.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Which use case needs a value other than shut-down and in-production, and what does each other value do differently at the next start?

precedents.title: Add DB_IN_END_OF_RECOVERY_CHECKPOINT state for control file

critic.reasoning: The docs give all five non-default values one effect, and the thread shows a use for only one. [P5] proposed a new DBState value, so the concern that the enum may change has support.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: Six raw pg_control states exposed where only forced crash recovery is shown
other_surviving.failure_scenario: An operator follows the docs and resets with --cluster-state=shut-down-in-recovery to empty unlogged tables. Startup code that groups DB_SHUTDOWNED_IN_RECOVERY with a clean shutdown may skip the crash-only steps, so the tables keep their stale contents. The operator finds out only when queries return rows that should have been reset.
other_surviving.argument: The docs and commit message say that every non-default state makes the next start run the same crash recovery, but startup in xlog.c handles DB_SHUTDOWNED_IN_RECOVERY next to DB_SHUTDOWNED in places, and DB_IN_ARCHIVE_RECOVERY is linked to minRecoveryPoint, which a reset clears. The test covers only in-production; message #5 confirms the six states are stored, not how startup treats each one. [P5] shows startup logic depends on exact state semantics, and this option would turn those internal assumptions into a user-facing contract. A single switch that forces crash recovery would match the only use case in message #1.
other_surviving.author_must_show: What does startup do differently for each of the five non-default states, or why not expose a single force-crash-recovery switch instead of the DBState enum?

precedents.title: Add DB_IN_END_OF_RECOVERY_CHECKPOINT state for control file

critic.reasoning: As far as I know, startup enters recovery for any state other than shut-down, so the stale-unlogged scenario is doubtful. But shut-down-in-recovery skips the crash-only data directory sync, so the states differ and the docs say they behave alike.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

refuted.title: Six exposed states rest on startup assumptions nobody has checked
refuted.failure_scenario: A DBA resets a crashed cluster with --cluster-state=shut-down-in-recovery and expects the documented effect, that unlogged tables are emptied. Startup code may treat that state as a clean shutdown and skip the unlogged reset. The DBA then finds stale unlogged data in production with no warning.
refuted.argument: [P5] died partly because a change to control file state was not checked against assumptions that depend on it, such as unlogged relation reset needing a clean shutdown, and minRecoveryPoint handling in DB_IN_ARCHIVE_RECOVERY. This patch exposes six states, but its docs say all non-default states behave alike, and its test covers only in-production (message #5 checked only that the states are stored). The thread does not say how startup treats shut-down-in-recovery, or in-archive-recovery after pg_resetwal has cleared the recovery fields.
refuted.author_must_show: For each of the six accepted states, what does the next startup do after a reset, and why expose any state beyond in-production?

precedents.title: Add DB_IN_END_OF_RECOVERY_CHECKPOINT state for control file

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1, which makes the same point about unchecked startup behaviour for each state and also names the single-switch alternative.

refuted.title: Dry-run state names differ from pg_controldata's spelling of the same field
refuted.failure_scenario: A DBA compares pg_controldata output, which says the state is "in production", with pg_resetwal --dry-run output, which says "in-production" for the same field. A monitoring or upgrade script that matches the pg_controldata strings fails to match the new pg_resetwal line.
refuted.argument: Message #4 says the new dry-run lines use the option's hyphenated names. pg_controldata already prints this field with space-separated names, so the project would show one value in two spellings. [P1] records that pg_resetwal output is read by pg_upgrade and possibly by external tools, so changes to it need care. The proposal does not say why the dry-run lines should not reuse the pg_controldata label and wording.
refuted.author_must_show: Why should the new dry-run lines not use the same label and state wording that pg_controldata prints today?

precedents.title: Revert ill-considered change in pg_resetwal output.

critic.reasoning: The dry-run state lines are new, so no existing script matches them, and [P1] concerns changing existing output strings. Message #4 gives a reason for the spelling: the lines use the names the option takes.

refuted.title: One shown use case does not justify six user-settable states
refuted.failure_scenario: Core ships six `--cluster-state` values, but only `in-production` has a known purpose, which is to empty unlogged tables after a forced reset. A DBA picks `in-archive-recovery` or `shut-down-in-recovery` because the docs list them. The next start behaves in a way no one has described, and the DBA finds out only at startup.
refuted.argument: Message #1 says that resetting unlogged tables is the only use the author has, and asks Michael what he had in mind. The thread has no answer to that question (messages #2 to #5). Reviewers tested the mechanics but did not argue for demand. [P12] was turned down because narrow use cases did not justify ongoing doc and maintenance cost, and the same weighing applies to five of the six values here.
refuted.author_must_show: Which real recovery situations need each non-default state, and would a single switch that forces crash recovery cover them?

precedents.title: pg_replslotdata - a tool for displaying replication slot information

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of demand-2, which makes the same point without relying on [P12]. [P12] weighed a whole new tool, which is a larger cost than values of one option.

refuted.title: Internal DBState enum becomes a stable command-line interface
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch adds, renames or changes the meaning of a DBState value, or makes startup rely on a state only appearing together with a signal file. Nothing checks that pg_resetwal's value list and docs still match, and nothing catches that a hand-set state now breaks a startup assumption. Users find out in a damaged recovery.
refuted.argument: The option maps one-to-one onto the DBState enum, so every value becomes a documented spelling that the project must keep. Startup code may assume that a state arrived through a normal shutdown or recovery path. [P5] shows that unlogged relation reset and minimum recovery point checks depend on those state transitions. The tests cover only `in-production` and a bad value, so the other four states have no guard.
refuted.author_must_show: What does startup do for each of the six states when pg_resetwal sets it, and how will a future DBState change keep this option correct?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1 for the enum-as-interface point and of replication-ondisk-1 for the startup assumptions. Its own scenario, a "damaged recovery", names no concrete case.

refuted.title: No user need shown beyond one unlogged-table case
refuted.failure_scenario: A committer adds a permanent pg_resetwal option to its documented surface and keeps it in its tests. The only stated user is a DBA who resets WAL on a crashed cluster and wants unlogged tables emptied. That DBA can already get this, so the option is kept for years with no known user.
refuted.argument: Message #1 says the unlogged-table case is "the only use I have so far" and asks Michael what he had in mind. Message #4 does not answer that question. No field report, -general or -bugs thread, or production story appears in the material. Testers in messages #2 and #5 confirmed that the patch works, not that anyone needs it. A rare post-reset case can also be handled by truncating unlogged tables, or by starting with no connections, stopping in immediate mode and starting again.
refuted.author_must_show: Which users run pg_resetwal on crashed clusters with unlogged tables, and why is truncating those tables after the reset not enough for them?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of already-exists-1, which states the same lack of shown need and describes the existing alternatives more concretely.

How do in-archive-recovery and shut-down-in-recovery behave on a standby, or with standby.signal or recovery settings present?

committability.owner_note: It needs a committer who knows the startup and recovery code and how it reads the pg_control state. None has posted in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for six documented state names tied to DBState, and for what startup does with each hand-set state, in every later release.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 within days of the reviews and answered both reviewers, which suggests he stays engaged.

not_now.evidence_that_would_change_it: A stated use case that the start, immediate stop and start sequence cannot serve, such as the motivation behind the original suggestion or a field report. For the extra values, one concrete case per state, or a reduction to a single switch that forces crash recovery.

priority.reason: The patch is small and confined to pg_resetwal, but it serves one rare post-reset case and exposes six enum values where one is used. A single switch that forces crash recovery, with a stated use case, would be cheaper to carry.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert ill-considered change in pg_resetwal output.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert ill-considered change in pg_resetwal output.
Reverted commit(s): Use the terminology "WAL file" not "log file" more consistently.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 31dcfae83 changed one pg_resetwal output string, and a
corresponding test in pg_upgrade, without sufficient thought for
the consequences.  We can't change that output without creating
hazards for cross-version upgrades, since pg_upgrade needs to be able
to read the output of several different versions of pg_resetwal.
There may well be external tools with the same requirement.

For the moment, just revert those two changes.  What we really
ought to do here is have a separate, stable, easily machine-readable
output format for pg_resetwal and pg_controldata, as proposed
years ago by Alvaro.  Once that's in place and tools no longer
need to depend on the exact spelling of the human-readable output,
we can put back this change.

precedents_retrieved.summary:

This reverts commit 1d863c250461410e60c9ed5d3180f32336f4c3e2.

This broke specifying the data directory as a relative path.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
Reverted commit(s): Add redo LSN to pgstats files
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit b860848232aa, that was added as a prerequisite for
the support of pgstats data flush across checkpoints, linking a pgstats
file to a specific checkpoint redo LSN.

As reported, this is proving to be currently problematic when going
through a pg_upgrade, that does direct manipulations of the control file
in the new cluster.  The LSN stored in the pgstats file is not able to
cope with any changes done in the control file by pg_upgrade yet,
causing the pgstats file to be discarded when starting the new cluster
after overriding its redo LSN (one is a `pg_resetwal -l` where the new
cluster's start LSN is bumped by a hardcoded value of 8 segments, see
copy_xact_xlog_xid).

The least painful path going forward is likely going to be a refactor of
the pgstats code so as it is possible to read and write some of its data
with some routines in src/common/, so as pg_upgrade or pg_resetwal are
able to update its data.  The main point is that we are going to need a
LSN in the stats file should we make it written at checkpoint time and
not only as part of a shutdown sequence.  It is too late to dive into
these details for v18, so let's revert the change, and let's try to
figure out all the details in the next release cycle.  The pgstats file
is currently only written as part of a shutdown sequence, and its
contents are still lost on crash, same as older releases.

Bump PGSTAT_FILE_FORMAT_ID.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add recovery to pg_control and remove backup_label
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Robert Haas, Andres Freund, Michael Paquier
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch removes backup_label and stores the recovery information in pg_control instead. pg_backup_stop() returns an updated pg_control as bytea for the backup software to store, which also avoids copying a torn pg_control.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas objected to changing the backup API again and asked for more senior votes before a change this large. Andres Freund (his view is visible only in quoted replies) stayed on the fence, saying it helps pg_basebackup but not external backups and removes a human-readable file used for debugging. Once incremental backup was committed and depended on backup_label, Michael Paquier proposed returning the entry, and the author withdrew it rather than rework the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: It would be a lot of work with all the new changes for incremental backup and since Andres and Robert appear to be very against the idea, I doubt it would be worth the effort.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add DB_IN_END_OF_RECOVERY_CHECKPOINT state for control file
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch stops the end-of-recovery checkpoint from setting the control file state to DB_SHUTDOWNING and then DB_SHUTDOWNED, which the author considered wrong. Two variants were posted: one adds a new state DB_IN_END_OF_RECOVERY_CHECKPOINT, and one keeps DB_IN_CRASH_RECOVERY or DB_IN_ARCHIVE_RECOVERY until DB_IN_PRODUCTION.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier argued that the current state is not incorrect, because an end-of-recovery checkpoint is a shutdown checkpoint and the code has relied on that for about 10 years. He said the change was not checked against other assumptions, such as unlogged relation reset needing a clean shutdown, and that it leaves an invalid minimum recovery point in DB_IN_ARCHIVE_RECOVERY. He added that it would make back-patching harder in a sensitive area, and the entry was closed after the thread went quiet.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This
patch would bring some extra visibility for something that's not
incorrect either on HEAD, as end-of-recovery checkpoints are the same
things as shutdown checkpoints.

precedents_retrieved.title: Query Jumbling for CALL and SET utility statements
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch made pg_stat_statements compute a query ID by jumbling CALL and SET statements, so calls that differ only in constants share one entry. This was meant to cut LWLock contention under track_utility; later versions added 2PC and savepoint commands.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers found no clear reason to jumble some utility statements and not others, and preferred jumbling all of them with code generated from the node definitions. Michael Paquier also worried about the cost of jumbling frequent transaction commands. The thread then stalled, and he returned the patch because the generated-code approach did not exist yet.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: So, this thread has stalled for the last few weeks and it seems to me that the conclusion is that we'd want an approach using a set of scripts that automate the generation of the code in charge of the DDL jumbling.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add control-C support for some psql meta-commands
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets control-C cancel the password prompt in psql's \password by passing psql's SIGINT longjmp target and enable flag down through simple_prompt() to pg_get_line_append(). The author planned to use the same mechanism for \prompt and \connect later.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Tom Lane's review comments were addressed in v2 and v3, and the last message posts v3 on the day the entry was withdrawn.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix pg_rewind false positives caused by shutdown-only WAL
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes how pg_rewind finds the end of WAL on the target, so that a shutdown checkpoint written after the divergence point does not by itself make a rewind necessary. pg_rewind would scan backward from the last checkpoint to the last record that is not shutdown-related.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas objected to the premise. The shutdown checkpoint updates the control file, and that change matters when deciding whether servers are in sync. Even if pg_rewind ignored those records, the restarted old primary still refuses to follow the new timeline. He also noted that the patch did not skip the RUNNING_XACTS record and did not check the rmgr ID, and he saw no workaround; a later patch from another poster got no reply before the entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: But I do not think we can do that, because (1) those WAL records might do important things like update the control file and (2) the server will not be OK with ignoring those WAL records even if pg_rewind decides that they are not important.

precedents_retrieved.title: psql: Allow editing query results with \gedit
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Pavel Stehule, Tom Lane, Robert Haas
precedents_retrieved.summary: A new psql meta-command, \gedit, opens the result of a single-table select in an editor as JSON. On save, psql compares the edited data with the original by primary key and sends the differences as UPDATE, INSERT and DELETE commands.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Pavel Stehule and Tom Lane found the feature too magical and risky: psql applies the generated commands without showing them, and it detects the table by naive query parsing. Tom Lane also said that INSERT and DELETE detection is ambiguous and that editing JSON is a poor interface for changing data. Robert Haas rejected the patch because users would hit cases that fail for unclear reasons, and the visible votes were mostly against it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: But I also do understand why the reactions thus far have been skeptical: there's a lot of pretty magical stuff in this patch.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "graceful shutdown" changes for Windows.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "graceful shutdown" changes for Windows.
Reverted commit(s): On Windows, close the client socket explicitly during backend shutdown.; On Windows, also call shutdown() while closing the client socket.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commits 6051857fc and ed52c3707 in HEAD (they were already
reverted in the back branches).  Further testing has shown that while
those changes do fix some things, they also break others; in particular,
it looks like walreceivers fail to detect walsender-initiated connection
close reliably if the walsender shuts down this way.  A proper fix for
this seems possible but won't be done in time for v15.

precedents_retrieved.title: Detectable crashes and unlogged table resets
precedents_retrieved.summary: The thread started with a per-table flag in the init fork so applications could detect that an unlogged table was reset after a crash, mainly for sharded setups where one shard can be lost. It moved to a server-wide record in pg_control of the last crash recovery (LSN, time and a counter), read through a SQL function, with an attached patch.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Discussion stopped after June 2021 with open questions: whether LSN or timestamp is useful (Tom Lane doubted LSN), whether to reset the counter, and whether to track promotions. The entry moved through four commitfests with no further activity, and Michael Paquier closed it because it had been idle too long.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This is too long, so let's discard this patch for now.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_replslotdata - a tool for displaying replication slot information
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Andres Freund, Michael Paquier, Julien Rouhaud
precedents_retrieved.summary: A new client-side tool, pg_replslotdata, reads the binary replication slot files under pg_replslot/ and prints slot information such as restart LSN, xid, slot type and two-phase state. It works while the server is down, in the same way as pg_controldata and pg_waldump.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Committers judged that the use cases did not justify the cost of maintaining a separate tool in core, including its documentation and translations, and that most needs can be met with an online server. Since the tool is entirely client side, reviewers suggested keeping it in an external repository. The author agreed to drop the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Weighed against the cost of maintaining (including documentation) a separate
tool this doesn't seem sufficient reason.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add more TAP coverage for archive status with crash recovery of standbys
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Add more TAP coverage for archive status with crash recovery of standbys
Reverted commit(s): Remove some unstable parts from new TAP test for archive status check
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This part of the test was included originally in 4e87c48, but got
reverted as of f9c1b8d because of timing issues in the test, where,
after more analysis, we found that the standbys may not have recovered
from the archives all the segments needed by the test.  This stabilizes
the test by making sure that standbys replay up to the position returned
by pg_switch_wal(), meaning that all segments are recovered before the
manual checkpoint that tests WAL segment recycling and its interactions
with archive status files.

precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 086221cf6b1727c2baed4703c582f657b7c5350e, which
was made to master only.

The approach implemented in the above commit has some issues.  While
those could easily be fixed incrementally, doing so would make
backpatching considerably harder, so instead first revert this patch.

roaster_notes.note: The proposal changes no existing pg_resetwal output, so [P1] does not apply. [P11] lapsed from inactivity. Message #1 points to an earlier suggestion by Michael, but the thread does not say what it was meant to solve.
Two objections from the standards and compatibility angle. Existing users are unaffected, because the default stays shut-down.

The only persistent state touched is the state field of pg_control. WAL format, catalogs, wire protocol and ABI do not change. The new dry-run line adds output without changing existing strings, so the pg_upgrade parsing concern in [P1] does not apply.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. pg_resetwal runs offline as the owner of the data directory, who can already rewrite pg_control or delete unlogged relation files directly, so --cluster-state gives no user an ability they lack today.
Two objections raised; the change is small and confined to pg_resetwal, so hot-path cost and external dependencies are not concerns.
One objection from this angle; no existing tool sets an arbitrary pg_control state, so only the demonstrated use case is covered.
Demand is the gap here. The option works as tested, but the thread shows one use case and an open question to the person who suggested it.
